summary: Laura Snapes in The Guardian walks through the most shocking moments in Britney Spears' memoir, The Woman in Me. The book recounts a life of constant scrutiny, a public body, a marketed virginity, and the 13-year conservatorship controlled by her father, including a two-month forced rehab stay she compares to ritual torture. It also covers her relationships with Justin Timberlake and her family, motherhood, music, and her path to freedom in November 2021.
one_line: A Guardian rundown of the most shocking revelations in Britney Spears' memoir The Woman in Me, centred on her 13-year conservatorship and loss of freedom.
key_facts: Britney Spears lived under a conservatorship controlled by her father for 13 years; she was granted her freedom in November 2021.
In June 2021 Spears called 911 to report her father for conservatorship abuse, days before a probate court hearing on the arrangement.

After objecting to a new dance move suggested for her Vegas residency, Spears was sent to a solitary rehabilitation facility for two months, where she was put on lithium and says she felt 'ritually tortured'.
Spears says her father told her 'I am Britney Spears now' when he seized legal control.
Under the conservatorship her dates had to agree to background checks and blood tests, sign NDAs, and receive a full rundown of her sexual history before the first date.
Her father would not let her remove her IUD to start a family with boyfriend, later husband, Sam Ashgari; they have divorced since she completed the memoir.
Spears was marketed as a virgin as a teenager, though she writes she first slept with her older brother's best friend at 14.
She describes being encouraged by Justin Timberlake and others to abort their pregnancy at home, with no pain relief, so no one would see them at a hospital.
Spears shaved her head in a salon in 2007, framing it as a 'fuck you' to impossible beauty standards.
She became pregnant a second time three months after giving birth to her first son, suffered severe postnatal depression, and says she felt suicidal.
Spears says the time she had the most passion for music was recording Baby, One More Time; she says she has no plans to make music at the moment.
After returning from the rehab facility she found her parents had thrown away her childhood things, including a binder of her poetry, and she decided she never wanted to see them again.
